subject: Intermittent API connection drops affecting chunked responses — customer briefing & postmortem plan
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@cedarbrooklabs.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cedarbrook SRE <sre@cedarbrooklabs.com>
Date: Sat, 26 May 2028 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Intermittent connection drops and truncated chunked responses

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

We're seeing a surge of failed requests from our integration with Redwood's hosted API in the last hour. Symptoms: many generation responses arrive partially (truncated last chunks) or the client sees a connection reset mid-stream. We've captured ~120 request IDs across a 30-minute window; example request IDs: rwd-7f3a-11, rwd-7f3a-34, rwd-7f3a-98. Error codes observed on our side: ECONNRESET, 502 (upstream reset).

This is impacting our chat product (live agent handoffs). Time window: ~17:50-18:10 PDT. We're routing retries aggressively which amplifies the effect on our side. Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing increased connection resets or if there is a known degradation in token streaming?

I've attached a tarball of tcpdumps and app logs for the affected requests. Attachment: cedarbrook_trace_0526.tar.gz (log bundle, ~8MB)

We'd appreciate an interim status update and any mitigation steps we can take while you triage.

Thanks,
Asha Patel
Head of Integrations
Cedarbrook Labs
asha.patel@cedarbrooklabs.com

Subject: Re: [URGENT] Intermittent connection drops and truncated chunked responses

Hi Asha — thanks for the quick signal and for attaching the traces.

On Sat, May 26, 2028 at 6:12 PM Asha Patel <asha.patel@cedarbrooklabs.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a surge of failed requests from our integration with Redwood's hosted API in the last hour...

We've escalated to ops and engineers and have an active incident (IR-20280526-7GJ3) open on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/IR-20280526-7GJ3. Irene is leading triage. Immediate ask: could you share a couple of full request/response pairs (headers + bodies) for 2-3 failing request IDs so we can correlate traces? If you prefer, we can open a short Zoom to review logs.

Temporary mitigations we're rolling out now:
- Route Cedarbrook traffic to a fallback pool with different batching configuration to reduce tokenization contention.
- Enable conservative client-side retries on our side to avoid amplifying transient resets.

We'll post regular updates to the status page and reply here. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

— Rafael
Head of Customer Success Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@cedarbrooklabs.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@cedarbrooklabs.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 May 2028 19:25:00 -0700
Subject: [Redwood Ops] Interim report — root cause hypothesis and mitigation timeline

Asha / Samir — quick update from ops and infra: we observed elevated socket CLOSE/RESET rates originating in our tokenization worker pool between 17:48 and 19:18 PDT. Preliminary indicators:
- A small subset of batching keys produced oversized input sequences causing tokenization stalls, which backed up worker queues and triggered connection timeouts for active streaming sessions.
- The backlog produced an amplification effect: retries and longer-lived connections increased memory pressure on the pool.

Mitigations applied at 19:22 PDT:
- Shifted Cedarbrook traffic to a reserved fallback pool with more conservative batch thresholds (decreased max batch size, shorter batching window).
- Recycled 3 tokenization workers to reclaim stalled threads.
- Temporarily increased connection timeout threshold for streaming responses to avoid mid-chunk resets while we stabilize.

Impact window (observed): ~17:48 - 19:22 PDT. During the peak we estimate 6–9% of Cedarbrook's requests experienced partial/truncated streams. After mitigation we saw connection resets fall back to baseline within ~20 minutes.

Next steps and commitments:
- We'll produce a written postmortem and a remediation plan by EOD tomorrow (May 27).
- Engineering will add input-size-based gating to the batching layer to prevent oversized sequences from stalling tokenizers.
- We'll offer a usage credit to Cedarbrook for the impacted window; Rafael will confirm terms with your billing contact.

On Sat, May 26, 2028 at 6:22 PM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We've escalated to ops and engineers and have an active incident (IR-20280526-7GJ3) open on our status page...

I'll keep this thread updated as we complete the initial RCA.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@cedarbrooklabs.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@cedarbrooklabs.com>

Date: Sun, 27 May 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary, next steps, and credits

Hi Asha / Samir — follow-up from our EOD review and the postmortem draft attached. Attachment: postmortem-summary-cedarbrook-20280527.pdf

Executive summary:
- Impact: intermittent streamed responses truncated or suddenly closed for Cedarbrook traffic. Peak impact window: 2028-05-26 17:48–19:22 PDT. Estimated affected request rate: ~7% of Cedarbrook's traffic during the window.
- Root cause: batching layer allowed oversized input groups to enter tokenization workers without input-size gating; oversized sequences stalled the worker's tokenizer loop and caused socket timeouts.
- Immediate fix: traffic reroute to fallback pool and worker recycle (19:22 PDT) — reduced resets to baseline by ~19:45 PDT.

Remediation plan (high level):
1) Batching hardening (priority P0): add input-size gating and per-batch token caps (owner: Evelyn Hart) — deploy target: 2028-06-07.
2) Streaming resiliency (P1): graceful per-connection backpressure to avoid mid-chunk resets (owner: Irene Choi) — deploy target: 2028-06-14.
3) Observability (P1): add streaming chunk-level tracing to make post-incident correlation faster (owner: Marissa Cole) — deploy target: 2028-06-21.

Credits and administration:
- Ben Carter from Billing will apply a pro-rated usage credit covering the impacted window; I'll loop Ben offline to confirm amount and timing.

Action items we own and immediate asks for Cedarbrook:
- We will run a short coordinated test next week (target: week of 6/3) to validate the batching gate in a staging environment with your integration team.
- Please send the two sample request/response pairs when convenient (Samir mentioned you would).

Links and artifacts:
- Incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/IR-20280526-7GJ3
- Postmortem draft (read-only): https://drive.google.com/file/d/pm-cedarbrook-20280527
- Support ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-1234

If this summary looks right, we'll finalize the postmortem and schedule the remediation rollout. Thanks for your collaboration and patience.

— Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Success Engineering
